questions.question: What upgrade does the manufacturer offer to raise this turbine's energy output, and by how much?
questions.truth: Siemens Gamesa EnergyUp sheet: software upgrade raising MM92 output to 2.2 MW (50 Hz), AEP up to 5%, only for turbines with a Bachmann controller.

baseline.answer: The EnergyUp Full Power Curve Advanced upgrade is compatible with the MM82, MM92, and MM100 turbines. This upgrade increases the Annual Energy Production (AEP) by optimizing torque and rotor speed. Specifically, for the MM92 turbine, the power output can be increased to 2.2 MW (for the 50 Hz market) and 2.125 MW (for the 60 Hz market). The AEP boost from this upgrade can be up to 5% depending on the turbine model and wind farm conditions.

final.answer: The manufacturer offers an upgrade called "EnergyUp Full Power Curve Advanced" for the Senvion MM92 turbine model. This upgrade increases the Annual Energy Production (AEP) by up to 5% (EnergyUp Full Power Curve Advanced - Senvion technology (MM82, MM92, MM100 upgrade), p.1). The power output is increased to 2.2 MW for the MM82 and MM92 (50 Hz market) (EnergyUp Full Power Curve Advanced - Senvion technology (MM82, MM92, MM100 upgrade), p.1).

questions.diagnosis: Right upgrade, 2.2 MW and up to 5%, but uncited, and it drops the sheet's scope note (only turbines with a Bachmann controller).
questions.fix: Citations now kept. The scope note is still dropped despite an explicit prompt rule: a remaining Nova Lite failure.

questions.question: What does an applicant have to submit in the ScotWind leasing round?
questions.truth: Crown Estate Scotland, ScotWind Leasing April 2019 update.

baseline.answer:
The ScotWind leasing round requires applicants to submit several key documents and information. I will present this information as per the technical documents found. </thinking>
Here is what an applicant has to submit in the ScotWind leasing round, according to the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.2:

- Project concept
- Project delivery plan
- Capability and experience
- Development budget
- Developer financial resources
- Commitment to the project and preparedness

Additionally, applicants may be asked to complete an application form and provide separate substantive documents, including those outlined in Table 1 of the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.2. If an application involves more than one legal entity, statements of commitment at board level are required (ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.2).

You can find more details in the ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft): https://www.crownestatescotland.com/sites/default/files/2023-07/scotwind-leasing-april-2019-update.pdf

final.answer:
An applicant has to submit the following in the ScotWind leasing round:

- Project concept
- Project delivery plan
- Capability and experience
- Development budget
- Developer financial resources
- Commitment to the project and preparedness

Additionally, the applicant is likely to be asked to provide the following documents:

- Detailed development budget
- Documentary evidence of nearby windfarm tenants' consent if applicable
- Information about all organizations responsible for any part of the project funding
- Statements of Commitment from the Lead and Sole Applicant, or from the Lead Applicant and all Project Partners, at Board level or equivalent

(ScotWind Leasing - April 2019 update (working draft), p.1-5)

questions.diagnosis: Right six areas, but leaked a '</thinking>' tag and a sentence of planning. Later runs also padded each item with invented explanations, or returned an empty answer.
questions.fix: Reasoning tags stripped, a rule against explanations the page doesn't give, and one retry on an empty reply. The final answer cites the whole document (p.1-5) where p.2 and p.4 would be exact.

questions.question: How close does the best turbine get to the Betz limit?
questions.truth: rank_turbines('peak_cp'): HillOfTowie_18's peak Cp 0.5995 is above the 0.593 Betz limit, which is physically impossible: a measurement artifact (anemometer reading low), not a near-Betz turbine.

baseline.answer: The turbine HillOfTowie_18 gets closest to the Betz limit with a peak Cp of 0.5995.

final.answer: The best turbine, HillOfTowie_18, reaches a peak power coefficient (Cp) of 0.599, which is slightly over the Betz limit of 0.593. This is an anomaly, as it is physically impossible for a turbine to exceed the Betz limit. The over-Betz reading is likely due to a nacelle anemometer bias, as indicated in the anomalies report.

questions.diagnosis: Called HillOfTowie_18 'closest to the Betz limit' with Cp 0.5995, which is above it: a physically impossible value presented as a success. Later runs named the second-highest turbine from the unsorted list.
questions.fix: Tools now flag a peak Cp above 0.593 as a measurement artifact (nacelle anemometer bias), and the analysis tool returns its extremes ready-made.
